text:
maria: heads-up: canary showing a p99 latency spike for rwd/gpt-small around 09:12 UTC. tokens/sec down ~30%. bench/latency failing on canary. tagging @eng-runtime :eyes:
aj: I see it too. Lots of compile requests queued on compile-worker-4. Looks like a compile 'storm' correlated with the spike. Kernel picker is choosing matmul_v3_fused for short seqs (seq=128,batch=8) instead of matmul_v2_tiled we usually use.
sam: that smells like the autotune heuristic shift. PRs touching kernel-autopick weights merged yesterday (PR #4122). Could be picking the wrong kernel for small batches.
bench-ci: bench/latency #987 failed on canary: p99=340ms (+120ms). Alert triggered.
nina: can someone paste repro steps and a quick profile? I can try to repro locally.
maria: repro used: ./bench --model rwd/gpt-small --seq 128 --batch 8 --profile --runs 200. Profile snippet below (trimmed):
```
PROFILE: compile_time_per_kernel_ms: matmul_v3_fused=28.4, matmul_v2_tiled=6.7
KV_CACHE: evictions=142, tombstones=7
KERNEL_PICK: matmul_v3_fused score=-0.3, matmul_v2_tiled score=-0.1
COMPILE_Q: compile_worker_4 queued=312 active=6
```
aj: thanks. The compile_time jump + evictions explain throughput drop. Important bit: the picker score math should have favored v2 for short sequences; score delta implies the heuristic weights flipped. Also seeing many cache invalidations — cache eviction policy changed in a separate PR recently?
sam: confirm: there was a small change to eviction thresholds in PR #4150 (cache tuning). Might be a bad interaction: more evictions -> more JIT compiles -> compile storm -> higher latency. But primary cause appears to be the autotune pick. I'm starting a git bisect on the autotune config repo.
ryan: oncall here. I'm going to pin canary to kernel variant v2 and roll back the autotune heuristic config as a hotfix to stop customer impact. Also will coordinate a deeper bisect. cc @eng-ml
deploy-bot: rollback initiated by ryan: reverting config cfg-autotune-20260315 -> cfg-autotune-20260314. Rolling back canary heuristic. ETA ~6m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
aj: quick note — PR #4122 changed the weight sign for short-seq penalty by accident (diff shows +0.2 vs -0.2). Likely a typo. Want to revert that as an immediate fix and follow up with tests.
sam: git bisect narrowed suspect to commit 0xabc123 (author: tzhao) that tweaked the short-seq scoring. Revert candidate: PR #4210 created (revert 0xabc123).
bench-ci: canary bench re-run queued.
maria: after rollback metrics are trending back to baseline. p99 down to ~210ms within 4 minutes. Keeping watch for 30m. :thumbsup:
aj: separate cleanup: we should revert the cache eviction tuning from PR #4150 in a follow-up if bisect shows it amplifies the problem. For now revert heuristic only.
ryan: agreed. Also let's add an integration test asserting kernel pick for the (seq=128,batch=8) case. This should run in bench/quick-regressions on CI.
nina: creating ENGRT-2314 to add the regression test + track follow-up for cache eviction change.
sam: drafting a short postmortem. Root cause: accidental sign/weight flip in autotune heuristic + cache eviction interaction -> compile storms and KV cache churn -> latency spike. Mitigations: stricter review & CI for autotune weight changes, add autotune pick unit tests, add canary gate that watches compile-queue length and auto-rollbacks, and revert-on-high-compile-rate feature.
maria: bench/latency passing on canary post-rollback. closing loop after monitoring window. Thanks everyone.
ryan: great catch. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-ml for follow-up.
bench-ci: bench/latency passed: p99=208ms. :white_check_mark:
